name: CJC-1295 with DAC

angle.text: CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting GHRH analogue used in growth hormone peptide stacks, with users aiming for better body composition, recovery, and skin. Forum posters debate combining it with ipamorelin or preferring the no-DAC version. Its effects on appearance have not been tested in trials.

summary: A long-acting GHRH analogue (drug affinity complex) talked about for growth hormone stacks; unapproved and with no appearance trials behind it.
note: Unapproved peptide; community talk rests on anecdote.
currentQuick:
CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting version of a GHRH analogue, meant to make the pituitary release more growth hormone. Forum users pair it with ipamorelin or tesamorelin for muscle and body-composition goals.
The community material is thin and anecdotal, and there are no cited trials of it for appearance.
How it works: It mimics GHRH at the pituitary, and the DAC attachment binds blood proteins to prolong its action versus the version without DAC.
Risks and caveats: It is not an approved medicine and risks in healthy users have not been defined by the sources used here. Forum discussions focus on combinations rather than safety data.
deepLead:
CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) that carries a drug affinity complex (DAC), a chemical attachment intended to bind blood proteins and prolong its action compared with shorter-acting GHRH analogues. It was developed by the Canadian company ConjuChem Biotechnologies and has not been approved as a medicine.
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities it is discussed as a growth hormone secretagogue for muscle, body composition and recovery, often together with a growth hormone-releasing peptide such as ipamorelin or with tesamorelin.  The community material available is limited to a small number of forum exchanges, in which users disagree about whether the DAC version or the version without DAC is preferable. 
No published human trials of its effect on appearance, muscle or body composition are cited here, so its appearance-related evidence is regarded as unproven.

name: Modified GRF (1-29)

angle.text: Mod GRF (CJC-1295 without DAC) is paired with a GHRP in forum stacks to boost growth hormone pulses, with users citing better sleep, recovery, and body composition. The synergy is described in hormone studies; human trials for appearance are absent.

summary: A short-acting GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 no DAC) paired with GHRPs in forum stacks; no human trials for appearance.
note: Seized products have contained modified (glycine-added) analogues.
currentQuick:
Modified GRF (1-29) is a lab-made fragment of GHRH tweaked to resist breakdown. Forum users inject it together with GHRP peptides in the hope of raising growth hormone for muscle and recovery.
No clinical trial cited here tests it for appearance, and user reports are anecdotal and mixed.
How it works: It stimulates GHRH receptors on pituitary cells to release growth hormone; the version without DAC is described as short-acting.
Risks and caveats: It is unapproved and listed as prohibited in sport per encyclopedia text. Forensic analysis of seized powders found glycine-added analogues, so contents of online products can differ from the label.
deepLead:
Modified GRF (1-29), also called Mod GRF, tetrasubstituted GRF (1-29) and CJC-1295 without DAC, is a synthetic 29-amino-acid analogue of the active fragment of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). Four amino acid substitutions are described as making it more resistant to enzymatic breakdown than the natural sequence.  It has not been approved as a medicine.
In bodybuilding and peptide forums it is typically described as the GHRH component of a pairing with a growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) such as GHRP-2, GHRP-6 or ipamorelin, with users reporting that the two together release more growth hormone than either alone. 
No published clinical trial cited here has tested Modified GRF (1-29) for muscle, fat loss or appearance. A Danish forensic study of seized doping powders found that products sold as modified GRF (1-29) and other secretagogues contained analogues with an extra glycine added, showing that the material sold online can differ from the labelled compound.

name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)

angle.text: GHRP-2 is used by peptide users to raise growth hormone for muscle growth, recovery, sleep, and sometimes height, and is preferred to GHRP-6 for causing less hunger. It is a real diagnostic agent in Japan; evidence that it builds muscle or height in healthy users is lacking.

summary: A potent ghrelin-receptor GH-releasing peptide: a real diagnostic in Japan, but nothing shows it builds muscle in healthy users.
note: Raises appetite and GH; no trials for appearance goals.
currentQuick:
GHRP-2 is a lab-made peptide that mimics ghrelin to trigger growth hormone release. It is used in Japan to test for GH deficiency, and in forums it is stacked with GHRH analogues for muscle and recovery.
Trials prove it raises GH, but none cited show better muscle or looks in healthy people.
How it works: It binds the ghrelin (GH secretagogue) receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, driving GH release through a path separate from GHRH.
Risks and caveats: Appetite and fat mass increases appear in animal studies, and long-term safety data for cosmetic use are lacking. It is not approved for body-composition use.
deepLead:
GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by acting on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor. It belongs to the family of growth hormone-releasing peptides developed from work led by Cyril Bowers at Tulane University and by Polygen in Germany. 
Medically, GHRP-2 is used in Japan as a diagnostic stimulation test for adult growth hormone deficiency.  Outside that test it is not an approved treatment. In bodybuilding and peptide communities it is used as a GH secretagogue, commonly alongside a GHRH analogue such as sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29), for muscle, recovery and body composition. 
Human studies establish that it releases GH, but no clinical trial cited here shows that it improves muscle or appearance in healthy people. A 2020 review of GH secretagogues in hypogonadal men notes that clinical efficacy data remain largely lacking.

name: Hexarelin (Examorelin)

angle.text: Hexarelin is regarded in peptide circles as the most potent GH-releasing peptide, used alone or with a GHRH analogue to build muscle with less water retention. It was studied in 1990s endocrine trials for hormone release; appearance effects are untested, and desensitization with repeated use is discussed.

summary: A potent GH-releasing peptide studied in 1990s endocrine trials; forum favourite, no evidence for looks, with desensitization questions.
note: Also hits cortisol and prolactin axes; GH response may fade.
currentQuick:
Hexarelin is a lab-made peptide that mimics ghrelin to force a big growth hormone release. Forum users pick it as a strong, cheap GH peptide for muscle and recovery.
Human trials measured hormone levels only; none tested muscle, fat or appearance.
How it works: It activates the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor, and also CD36 in the heart, driving GH release and effects on other hormones.
Risks and caveats: It also raises cortisol and prolactin in some studies, and a 16-week trial was built to test whether the GH response fades. It is not approved as a medicine.
deepLead:
Hexarelin (also called examorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by activating the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, the receptor for the gut hormone ghrelin.  Reviews describe it as more chemically stable and more potent than ghrelin itself. 
It has been studied in clinical endocrinology since the mid-1990s, including in healthy volunteers, people with GH deficiency and elderly adults.  It is not an approved medicine. In bodybuilding forums it is discussed as a potent, cheaper GHRP, often paired with a GHRH analogue. 
Published human studies have measured hormone responses, not muscle, fat or appearance outcomes. A 16-week study in healthy elderly people was designed to test whether the GH response weakens with long-term use, a limitation that the investigators described as potentially serious for therapeutic use.

name: Bimagrumab

angle.text: Bimagrumab is an investigational antibody that blocks activin receptors, and appearance communities follow it as a way to lose fat while preserving or adding muscle. Trials report fat loss with muscle preservation in people with obesity; it is not available outside studies.

summary: An investigational antibody that blocks muscle brakes; trials show fat loss and muscle preservation, but it is not available outside studies.
note: Investigational IV antibody; muscle mass gains did not clearly improve function in older adults.
currentQuick:
Bimagrumab is an antibody that blocks the activin receptors that limit muscle growth. In trials it increased lean mass and reduced fat, and Lilly is testing it with GLP-1 drugs to protect muscle during weight loss.
It is investigational only, given by infusion in trials, and not a product people can obtain legitimately.
How it works: It occupies ActRIIA/ActRIIB, preventing myostatin, activins and GDF11 from signalling, which allows muscle growth and affects fat tissue.
Risks and caveats: No approval exists. Reported side effects include muscle spasms, diarrhoea and acne according to an unverified AI-generated summary, and strength or function gains were not demonstrated in older adults.
deepLead:
Bimagrumab (BYM338, LY3985863) is an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody that blocks activin type II receptors (ActRIIA and ActRIIB), the receptors through which myostatin, activins and related signals restrain muscle growth.  It was developed by Novartis, and Eli Lilly acquired rights to it through its purchase of Versanis Bio in 2023, according to an AI-generated encyclopedia summary. 
It is not approved for any use. It has been trialled in sporadic inclusion body myositis, sarcopenia, recovery after hip fracture surgery, type 2 diabetes with obesity, and, more recently, obesity in combination with incretin drugs such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, where the goal is to lose fat while preserving muscle. 
A phase 2 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity reported significant loss of body fat and gain of lean mass over 48 weeks.  Trials in sarcopenia and inclusion body myositis increased muscle mass, but the benefit for strength or function was not shown, according to the AI-generated summary.  Its interest in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles stems from the "gain muscle while losing fat" profile; no community discussion of it was available for this entry.

name: Survodutide

angle.text: Survodutide is a once-weekly injectable followed by people interested in the next generation of weight-loss peptides. Phase 2 and 3 trials in obesity and fatty liver disease report weight loss, and it has not been approved; appearance effects arrive through fat loss.

summary: A glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist in phase 3; real weight-loss trials in obesity and liver disease, not yet approved.
note: Investigational; evidence is in patients, not cosmetic use.
currentQuick:
Survodutide is a weekly injection that activates glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. It is in phase 3 trials for obesity and liver disease, from Boehringer Ingelheim.
Phase 2 and 3 trials report weight loss in people with obesity, but it is not approved and has no cosmetic-use evidence.
How it works: GLP-1 activation reduces appetite while glucagon receptor activation is thought to raise energy expenditure and act on the liver.
Risks and caveats: Safety is still under evaluation in phase 3 and cardiovascular outcomes trials. As a GLP-1-class drug, questions include muscle, bone and gastrointestinal effects. It is not available as an approved medicine.
deepLead:
Survodutide (BI 456906) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the glucagon receptor and the GLP-1 receptor. It is being developed by Boehringer Ingelheim for obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and has not been approved as a medicine at the time of writing. 
Its logic is that adding glucagon-receptor activation, which is thought to raise energy expenditure and act on the liver, may produce more weight loss than GLP-1 receptor agonism alone.  Reviews group it with retatrutide and mazdutide among glucagon/GLP-1 co-agonists. 
Phase 2 trials have reported weight loss and liver benefits, and phase 3 results in obesity and in obesity with fatty liver disease were published in 2026.  No community discussion of it for appearance was available for this entry, and the evidence relates to medical weight management in people with obesity rather than cosmetic use.

name: VK2735

angle.text: VK2735 is an investigational GLP-1/GIP agonist watched by people seeking strong fat loss. Phase 2 reported roughly 9 to 15 percent weight loss in 13 weeks, and phase 3 is underway. Its effect on appearance comes through reduced body fat.

summary: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist in phase 3; phase 2 showed about 9 to 15% weight loss in 13 weeks, but it is still investigational.
note: Investigational; trials are in people with obesity, not cosmetic use.
currentQuick:
VK2735 is a weekly injectable (and oral form in trials) that activates the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, like tirzepatide. Viking Therapeutics is running phase 3 trials for obesity.
In a 13-week phase 2 study, people lost 9 to 15% of body weight on it versus about 2% on placebo.
How it works: It activates GLP-1 and GIP receptors to reduce appetite and affect metabolism, as other incretin-based weight-loss drugs do.
Risks and caveats: Safety is still being assessed in phase 3. It is not approved, and the 13-week trial was short, so long-term effects are unknown.
deepLead:
VK2735 is an investigational dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors, developed by Viking Therapeutics for weight management. It is being tested as a weekly subcutaneous injection and as a daily oral formulation, and is not approved as a medicine. 
It works on the same pair of receptors as tirzepatide, which is already approved. Reviews discuss new co-agonists of this type as more potent weight-loss drugs than GLP-1 agonism alone. 
In a 13-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight, mean weight loss ranged from 9.1% to 14.7% depending on dose, versus 1.7% with placebo.  Phase 3 trials started in 2025, and there is no evidence of use outside medical studies for appearance purposes.

name: CagriSema

angle.text: CagriSema is a weekly cagrilintide and semaglutide shot discussed by users chasing large fat loss, sometimes compared with retatrutide. Phase 3 trials showed weight loss of about 20 percent in people with obesity. It is not approved, and any effect on looks comes through fat loss.

summary: Not-yet-approved weekly semaglutide plus cagrilintide shot that cut weight about 20% in phase 3 trials.
note: Investigational; unapproved supply is unregulated. GI side effects common.
currentQuick:
CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that pairs semaglutide with cagrilintide, an amylin analogue. It is being developed by Novo Nordisk for obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Phase 3 trials report about 20% mean weight loss over 68 weeks in adults without diabetes, more than semaglutide alone but less than tirzepatide in one head-to-head comparison.
How it works: Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and cagrilintide activates amylin receptors; both reduce appetite and slow eating, through partly different pathways.
Risks and caveats: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are the most reported effects, and were more frequent than with semaglutide alone. It is an investigational drug without an approved label; any supply outside trials is unregulated.
deepLead:
CagriSema is an investigational once-weekly injectable combination of cagrilintide, an amylin receptor agonist, and semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, developed by Novo Nordisk for weight management . It is intended for adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes, and is not an appearance product in itself; any effect on looks comes through fat loss.
In a phase 3a trial in adults without diabetes, the combination produced a mean body-weight change of about 20% over 68 weeks versus about 3% with placebo . A meta-analysis of three early randomized trials found greater weight loss with the combination than with semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, together with more gastrointestinal adverse events . In a head-to-head open-label trial reported by the developer, it did not meet the non-inferiority endpoint against tirzepatide .
Per Grokipedia, a new drug application was filed with the US FDA in December 2025, and the product was not approved at the time of that source . In forum discussion, CagriSema is mentioned alongside other newer peptides such as retatrutide .

name: Exenatide

angle.text: Exenatide, the original GLP-1 shot, is mentioned by users as an early route to appetite control and fat loss, now overshadowed by semaglutide. Trials in type 2 diabetes show modest weight loss; its use for appearance is off-label.

summary: Original Gila-monster-derived GLP-1 shot for type 2 diabetes with only modest weight loss, long since eclipsed by semaglutide.
note: Diabetes drug, not licensed for weight loss; label warns of pancreatitis.
currentQuick:
Exenatide is the first GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for type 2 diabetes, in 2005. It is injected under the skin, either twice daily or once weekly.
It causes modest weight loss, but it is not approved for weight management and later GLP-1 drugs are reported to produce larger effects.
How it works: It mimics GLP-1: it raises insulin release when glucose is high, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying and reduces appetite. It is a synthetic version of a peptide found in Gila monster saliva.
Risks and caveats: The label warns of pancreatitis, low blood sugar when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas, kidney injury from dehydration and severe gastrointestinal effects. Nausea is common. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Exenatide is a synthetic peptide that activates the GLP-1 receptor and is approved in the United States as an adjunct to diet and exercise for adults with type 2 diabetes. It is based on exendin-4, a hormone first identified in the saliva of the Gila monster, and was first marketed as Byetta, a twice-daily injection, in 2005 . An extended-release once-weekly form, Bydureon, followed .
Exenatide is not licensed for weight loss. Trial and review data describe a modest weight reduction in people with type 2 diabetes, with Grokipedia citing an average of 2 to 3 kg over six months . It has since been overshadowed by later GLP-1 drugs such as liraglutide and semaglutide, which are reported to produce greater weight loss . In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it appears mostly as an early example of the class, in 2005 to 2009 threads on T Nation .

name: Tesofensine

angle.text: Tesofensine is promoted for strong appetite suppression and fat loss, and some users see it as an alternative to approved weight-loss drugs. A 24-week trial found weight loss beyond placebo of about 4.5 to 10.6 percent, with raised heart rate and blood pressure. It is not approved.

summary: Never-approved triple reuptake inhibitor that cut weight 4.5% to 10.6% beyond placebo in a 24-week trial, with heart-rate and blood-pressure rises.
note: Unapproved; raises heart rate and blood pressure; supply is unregulated.
currentQuick:
Tesofensine is an oral drug that was first tested for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. Participants lost weight, so the developer turned to obesity.
A 2008 phase II trial found weight loss exceeding placebo by about 4.5% to 10.6% over 24 weeks. It has not been approved by major regulators.
How it works: It blocks the reuptake of dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin, raising their levels in the brain. In animals this reduces appetite via hypothalamic circuits.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include dry mouth, nausea, insomnia and increased heart rate and blood pressure. Related drugs such as sibutramine were withdrawn for safety reasons. It is unapproved, and supply outside trials is unregulated.
deepLead:
Tesofensine (development code NS2330) is an investigational oral drug that blocks the reuptake of dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin. It was developed by the Danish company NeuroSearch, first for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, and then pursued as an obesity treatment after weight loss was observed in those trials .
In a 24-week phase II trial in 203 obese adults, published in The Lancet in 2008, placebo-adjusted weight loss ranged from about 4.5% to 10.6% across the three doses tested . Later work combined it with metoprolol (Tesomet) in rare forms of obesity . It is not approved by the US FDA or the European Medicines Agency for any use, and available reviews list it among drugs under development .
Reported adverse effects in the literature include dry mouth, nausea, insomnia and increases in heart rate and blood pressure . It is discussed on looksmax.org as a weight-loss option that users source outside regulated channels .

name: Orlistat

angle.text: Orlistat is used during cutting phases to absorb less dietary fat, and some describe it as a replacement for banned stimulants. Trials show a few kilos of weight loss over placebo, with oily stools as a known effect; it works less for people already eating low-fat.

summary: OTC and Rx fat-absorption blocker that adds a few kilos of weight loss over placebo at the price of oily stools.
note: GI side effects common; label warns against use with cyclosporine and after organ transplant.
currentQuick:
Orlistat is a capsule taken with meals that blocks the enzymes that digest dietary fat. The 60 mg Alli is sold over the counter; the 120 mg Xenical needs a prescription.
Trials show weight loss greater than placebo, but modest compared with newer injectable drugs; about 2 to 3 kg extra over 6 to 12 months is cited.
How it works: Orlistat inhibits lipase enzymes in the stomach and pancreas, so some of the fat in a meal is not absorbed and leaves in the stool. Very little enters the bloodstream.
Risks and caveats: Oily spotting, urgency, gas and loose stools are common, especially with fatty meals. It can reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, and the label warns against use after organ transplant or with cyclosporine.
deepLead:
Orlistat is a gastrointestinal lipase inhibitor used with a reduced-calorie diet for weight loss in adults. It is sold by prescription as Xenical (120 mg capsules) and over the counter as Alli (60 mg capsules), and it works inside the gut rather than being absorbed into the bloodstream . Reviews describe it as one of five or so drugs available for long-term obesity treatment in the US, with weight loss smaller than that of newer injectable drugs .
Trials such as the 1998 European multicentre study and a 2-year US trial found greater weight loss on orlistat than placebo . Grokipedia describes an average extra loss of about 2 to 3 kg over 6 to 12 months . The most commonly reported side effects are gastrointestinal, including oily spotting and urgency, reported in more than 25% of patients in one review .
In bodybuilding and fat-loss forums such as T Nation, orlistat is discussed as a fat blocker and was described in 2006 as a possible replacement for ephedrine . Some posters report diarrhea and little benefit .

name: Naltrexone/Bupropion (Contrave)

angle.text: Contrave is a prescription pill used for appetite control and weight management, followed by people seeking fat loss without injections. Trials show solid but modest weight loss compared with GLP-1 drugs. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

summary: Prescription pill pairing an opioid blocker with an antidepressant for appetite control; solid but modest weight loss next to GLP-1 drugs.
note: Prescription-only; bupropion carries warnings on mood and seizures.
currentQuick:
Contrave is a daily extended-release tablet combining naltrexone and bupropion. It is approved to help adults with obesity or overweight lose weight alongside diet and exercise.
Trials report weight loss over placebo, but network meta-analyses place it below semaglutide and tirzepatide.
How it works: Bupropion raises dopamine and noradrenaline and activates appetite-suppressing neurons in the hypothalamus, while naltrexone blocks the opioid feedback that would otherwise damp that effect, so the pair reduce appetite and cravings.
Risks and caveats: Reviews note constipation in about 20% of users of centrally acting weight drugs; nausea, headache and insomnia are also reported. Bupropion carries warnings about suicidal thoughts and seizure risk and can raise blood pressure. Prescription-only.
deepLead:
Naltrexone/bupropion, sold as Contrave (Mysimba in some markets), is a fixed-dose oral combination of an opioid-receptor antagonist and an antidepressant and smoking-cessation drug, approved for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight alongside diet and exercise . It is one of the centrally acting weight-loss drugs reviewed alongside phentermine-topiramate .
Phase 3 trials, including COR-I, COR-II and COR-BMOD, compared the sustained-release combination with placebo over about 56 weeks . Network meta-analyses rank it as producing smaller average weight loss than semaglutide or tirzepatide . A JAMA review lists constipation among adverse effects of centrally acting drugs in about 20% of patients .
The combination has also been studied for binge-eating disorder and methamphetamine use disorder . No community discussion specific to the drug appears in the sources reviewed.

name: Phentermine

angle.text: Phentermine is a decades-old prescription appetite suppressant used for short-term weight loss and cutting. Trials show modest weight loss over a few weeks to months, and it appears in many forum fat-loss stacks. The appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

summary: Decades-old prescription stimulant appetite suppressant with short-term, modest weight loss and cardiovascular warnings.
note: Controlled stimulant; label warns of pulmonary hypertension and valve disease; contraindicated in pregnancy.
currentQuick:
Phentermine is a prescription stimulant that suppresses appetite and has been used for short-term weight loss since 1959. It is the most prescribed obesity drug in the US, according to reviews.
Weight loss is modest, about 3.6 kg over placebo at 12 weeks per one summary, and smaller than with newer injectable drugs.
How it works: It is an amphetamine-like sympathomimetic amine that releases norepinephrine in the brain, which reduces hunger.
Risks and caveats: Labels warn of rare pulmonary hypertension and valvular heart disease, and of effects like raised blood pressure, insomnia and dependence-related withdrawal. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and is a controlled substance. The fen-phen episode of the 1990s involved heart valve damage.
deepLead:
Phentermine is a sympathomimetic amine with an amphetamine-like profile, sold by prescription as an appetite suppressant and approved in the US as a short-term adjunct, usually described as a few weeks, to diet, exercise and behavior change in adults with obesity . Grokipedia dates its FDA approval to 1959 and lists brands including Adipex-P, Lomaira and Duromine .
Reviews report that it is the commonly prescribed and that it produces modest weight loss compared with newer incretin drugs; Grokipedia cites about 3.6 kg more than placebo over 12 weeks . It is also one of the two components of phentermine/topiramate (Qsymia), which was studied in the CONQUER, SEQUEL and EQUIP trials .
Phentermine is also remembered for the fenfluramine-phentermine (fen-phen) combination, which was linked to valvular heart disease in a 1997 report, leading to the withdrawal of fenfluramine . The US label lists rare pulmonary hypertension and valvular heart disease as warnings .

name: Phentermine/Topiramate (Qsymia)

angle.text: Qsymia is a once-daily capsule used for chronic weight management and discussed as a non-injection route to fat loss. Trials show clear weight loss over placebo, though less than GLP-1 injections. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

summary: Once-daily phentermine plus topiramate capsule with clear weight loss over placebo, though behind GLP-1 injections, and a pregnancy risk.
note: Topiramate component linked to birth defects; Rx-only.
currentQuick:
Qsymia pairs phentermine, a stimulant appetite suppressant, with topiramate, an anticonvulsant, in a single daily capsule. It was approved in 2012 and extended to adolescents in 2022.
Phase 3 trials show more weight loss than placebo, but newer injectable drugs outperform it in comparative analyses.
How it works: Phentermine raises norepinephrine release to reduce hunger, while topiramate is thought to add satiety and reduce appetite through other brain pathways. Together they are designed to lower appetite more than either alone.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include tingling, dry mouth, constipation, insomnia and cognitive slowing, and increased heart rate. Topiramate in pregnancy is associated with oral clefts. Prescription-only.
deepLead:
Phentermine/topiramate extended-release (Qsymia) is a fixed-dose capsule combining phentermine, a sympathomimetic amine, with topiramate, an anticonvulsant, taken once daily to reduce appetite and increase satiety . It was approved by the US FDA in 2012 for chronic weight management and in July 2022 became the first approved for pediatric use of this combination, as noted in a review of that approval . The marketer cited in that review is VIVUS .
Reviews describe it as one of the more effective of the older oral obesity drugs, although network meta-analyses of drugs place incretin-based injections ahead of it . Studies have also examined it in binge-eating disorder and bulimia, adolescents and after bariatric surgery .
Topiramate is associated with birth defects and the combination is reviewed for use in women of reproductive age with obesity .

name: Clenbuterol

angle.text: Clenbuterol is a gray-market cutting pill, said to give a shredded look, increase vascularity, and sometimes stacked with DNP. It was developed as an asthma drug, and a 1995 review noted athletes' use for purported fat loss and anabolic effects. Human evidence for those effects is limited.

summary: Asthma-drug stimulant used as a gray-market cutting pill, with a documented record of heart problems.
note: Not approved for humans in the US; case reports of arrhythmia, myocarditis and death; banned in sport.
currentQuick:
Clenbuterol is a beta-2 agonist made as an asthma bronchodilator. It is not approved for people in the US but is bought online by bodybuilders and others for fat loss.
The only randomized trial in healthy men reported added lean mass but poorer cardiorespiratory fitness.
How it works: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, which relax airways and, in muscle and fat tissue, are linked to protein accretion and fat breakdown. Receptors can become less responsive with repeated use.
Risks and caveats: Case reports in athletes describe fast heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, chest pain, myocarditis, heart attack and death. It is banned in sport and in food animals, and unregulated supply can be mislabeled or contaminated.
deepLead:
Clenbuterol is a long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist developed as a bronchodilator for asthma and airway obstruction. It is prescribed in some countries for respiratory disease and in veterinary medicine, mainly for horses, but it is not approved for human use in the United States . It is on prohibited-substance lists in sport, and a 1995 review described its popularity with athletes for purported anabolic effects and reduction of subcutaneous fat .
Its use for fat loss and muscle retention is outside any approved indication. Rodent studies from the 1980s reported effects on body composition and muscle growth , while a 2025 randomized trial in 11 healthy men found increased lean mass and muscle protein accretion alongside reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and desensitization of muscle beta-2 signalling . A systematic review of case reports in athletes described cardiac events including tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, myocarditis, myocardial infarction and death .
On looksmax.org, users discuss clenbuterol as a cheap fat-loss pill for getting lean, often compared with GLP-1 drugs and stacked with other compounds .

name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP)

angle.text: DNP is used by some bodybuilders as a fast cutting drug, with users reporting around 8 to 10 lb of fat loss in three weeks. It raises metabolic rate by uncoupling cells' energy production and was sold as a diet drug in the 1930s. Posters compare it with GLP-1 options.

summary: A 1930s diet drug that melts fat by turning cells into heaters; the narrow gap between effective and lethal is why it is banned for human use.
note: Fatal overheating with no antidote; regulated poison in the UK since 2023; banned by WADA.
currentQuick:
DNP is an industrial chemical that was sold as a diet pill in the 1930s before being judged too toxic. It reappeared in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles as a very fast fat burner, with users reporting several pounds lost per week.
Evidence for its fat-loss effect is historical and anecdotal; no modern controlled trials exist. The mechanism is well understood, but the safety margin is described as very narrow.
How it works: DNP shuttles protons across the mitochondrial membrane, so cells burn fuel and release the energy as heat instead of making ATP. Metabolic rate rises, and so does body temperature.
Risks and caveats: Reported harms include overheating (hyperthermia) up to fatal temperatures, cataracts, rash, and blood and organ damage. There is no antidote. It is not approved for human use; the UK made it a regulated poison in 2023, a seller has been convicted of manslaughter, and WADA bans it.
deepLead:
2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP) is a yellow crystalline industrial chemical that has been used in explosives, pesticides and dyes, and that was briefly sold as a weight-loss drug in the United States in the 1930s . It acts as a mitochondrial uncoupler: it makes cells release energy as heat rather than storing it as ATP, which raises metabolic rate .
In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, DNP is discussed as a very fast fat-loss compound, and users on looksmax.org describe cutting cycles lasting from a couple of weeks to a few weeks, often alongside other compounds . It is not approved as a medicine anywhere that the sources describe; it is sold online as a research or industrial chemical .
Toxicology literature and regulators describe a very narrow gap between the doses that raise metabolism and doses that cause dangerous overheating (hyperthermia), and there is no specific antidote . Published clinical weight-loss trials meeting modern standards were not found; the evidence is historical case experience, toxicology reports and forum anecdote.

name: Ephedrine

angle.text: Ephedrine is the stimulant in the classic ECA stack, used for appetite suppression and energy during fasted cardio while cutting. Trials show modest fat loss, and it is a milder thermogenic than clenbuterol or DNP. Forum users also pair it with MK-677 to offset hunger.

summary: The stimulant in the classic ECA stack: modest fat loss in trials, but a pulse-and-pressure raiser that the FDA banned from supplements.
note: Raises heart rate and blood pressure; ephedrine-alkaloid supplements banned in the US since 2004.
currentQuick:
Ephedrine is a stimulant from Ephedra plants, used medically to raise blood pressure during anesthesia. In looksmaxxing it is known as the ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin (ECA) stack for cutting.

deepLead:
Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic amine and central nervous system stimulant found naturally in plants of the genus Ephedra (ma huang) and also made synthetically . It acts on adrenergic receptors and triggers release of norepinephrine, producing raised blood pressure, heart rate and alertness . In current US medical practice it is a prescription injectable indicated for clinically important hypotension during anesthesia .
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities ephedrine is discussed as a fat-loss and appetite-suppression aid, most often as the "ECA stack" of ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin . Guides on looksmax.org describe it as increasing energy and reducing hunger during a cut, and typically attach heart-health cautions .
A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis examined ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and athletic performance . A general reference summarises the clinical evidence as showing modest short-term weight loss of about 0.9 kg per month more than placebo, alongside increased heart rate and cardiovascular risk; the US FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements in 2004 .

name: Sibutramine

angle.text: Sibutramine is a withdrawn appetite suppressant that cutting forum users see as a substitute or complement to an ECA stack. Randomised trials found modest weight loss beyond diet and exercise. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

summary: A withdrawn prescription appetite suppressant that worked modestly for weight loss but raised cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.
note: Withdrawn in the EU and US in 2010 after the SCOUT cardiovascular trial; undeclared in some supplements.
currentQuick:
Sibutramine was a prescription weight-loss pill that made people feel full sooner. Trials showed it helped people lose a few kilograms more than diet alone.
It was withdrawn in 2010 after a large trial in high-risk patients found more heart attacks and strokes. It has little presence in looksmaxxing forums.
How it works: It blocks reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine in the brain, increasing feelings of fullness and reducing food intake.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include raised heart rate and blood pressure, dry mouth, insomnia and constipation, and a case report of psychosis. Regulators withdrew it in the EU and US in 2010.
deepLead:
Sibutramine, sold as Meridia (US) and Reductil (elsewhere), is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that was approved as an appetite suppressant for obesity and later withdrawn from major markets over cardiovascular safety concerns . Randomised trials found it produced modest weight loss beyond diet and exercise .
The 2010 SCOUT outcomes trial in more than 10,000 overweight or obese people with cardiovascular disease or diabetes led regulators to suspend or withdraw it . Looksmaxxing relevance is limited: the sources show only scattered mentions on bodybuilding forums such as T Nation, where users compared it with ECA stacks and other appetite suppressants before and after withdrawal . Sibutramine is also known as an undeclared ingredient in some weight-loss supplements .

name: Ketoconazole

angle.text: Ketoconazole shampoo (Nizoral) is added to finasteride and minoxidil routines in hair-loss communities for less shedding and a cleaner, calmer scalp, alongside its use for dandruff. Small studies hint at benefit for pattern hair loss; large trials are missing.

summary: Antifungal dandruff shampoo that hair-loss communities add to finasteride and minoxidil; small studies hint at benefit, large trials are missing.
note: Oral ketoconazole has a boxed warning for liver toxicity; the shampoo is the form used for hair.
currentQuick:
Ketoconazole is an antifungal. As a shampoo it treats dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, and many hair-loss forum members use it a couple of times a week as an add-on to finasteride and minoxidil.
A 2020 systematic review of five small human studies found increased hair shaft thickness and called it a promising adjunct. It has not been tested in large trials against standard treatments.
How it works: It blocks fungal cell-membrane synthesis, which reduces Malassezia yeast and scalp inflammation. Proposed antiandrogen effects on the scalp are discussed but not established.
Risks and caveats: The shampoo causes mild irritation, dryness or itching in a small share of users. Oral ketoconazole carries boxed warnings for liver injury and drug interactions and is restricted by the FDA.
deepLead:
Ketoconazole is a synthetic imidazole antifungal. It is available as oral tablets for serious fungal infections and as topical creams, foams and shampoos (such as Nizoral) for skin and scalp conditions including dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis and pityriasis versicolor .
In hair-loss communities, ketoconazole 2% shampoo is discussed as an adjunct to finasteride and minoxidil, on the theory that it may reduce scalp inflammation and local androgen activity. A 2020 systematic review of topical ketoconazole in androgenetic alopecia (AGA) called it a promising adjunctive treatment, based on five human studies (318 participants) and two animal studies . The US shampoo label lists dandruff-type and tinea versicolor indications, not hair loss .
Oral ketoconazole carries an FDA boxed warning for liver toxicity and other risks, whereas the shampoo is applied topically and is not detected in plasma after chronic scalp use according to its label .

name: Baricitinib

angle.text: Baricitinib is a prescription JAK inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition causing patchy or total hair loss. It is followed in hair communities for its regrowth results, and it is not approved for ordinary male pattern baldness.

summary: A prescription JAK inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata (autoimmune hair loss), not for ordinary pattern baldness, and carrying a boxed warning.
note: Boxed warning for serious infection, clots, cardiovascular events and cancer; evidence applies to alopecia areata only.
currentQuick:
Baricitinib is a once-daily pill that dampens the immune signalling behind alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy to total hair loss. It was FDA-approved for severe cases in adults in 2022.
Two phase 3 trials showed more regrowth than placebo at the higher dose. It is not tested or approved for common pattern baldness.
How it works: It blocks JAK1 and JAK2 enzymes, which relay inflammatory cytokine signals, reducing the immune attack on hair follicles.
Risks and caveats: The label carries a boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, cancer, major cardiovascular events and blood clots. Monitoring of blood counts, lipids and liver tests is required.
deepLead:
Baricitinib (brand name Olumiant) is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) 1 and 2 inhibitor developed by Incyte and Eli Lilly and approved for rheumatoid arthritis, severe alopecia areata and hospitalised COVID-19 . For hair, it is relevant to alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition causing patchy or total hair loss, rather than to common male pattern baldness .
In June 2022 the FDA approved baricitinib as the first systemic treatment for severe alopecia areata in adults, based on the BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 phase 3 trials . A European consensus statement notes that baricitinib and ritlecitinib are the only two EMA-approved medications for alopecia areata .
It carries a boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis . No community discussion of baricitinib for appearance was found in forum sources; it is included as a medically relevant hair-loss drug.
